+    def _is_all_any_call(self, node):
+        """Check if node is a call to all() or any() with a comprehension."""
+        if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
+            return None
+        if not isinstance(node.func, ast.Name):
+            return None
+        if node.func.id not in ('all', 'any'):
+            return None
+        if len(node.args) != 1:
+            return None
+        arg = node.args[0]
+        # Check if the argument is a generator expression or list/set comprehension
+        if isinstance(arg, (ast.GeneratorExp, ast.ListComp, ast.SetComp)):
+            return node.func.id
+        return None
+
+    def _unroll_all_any(self, assert_, all_any_name, comp_node):
+        """Unroll all()/any() calls into for loops with assertions."""
+        # comp_node is either GeneratorExp, ListComp, or SetComp
+        # All have the same structure: elt and generators
+        
+        # For now, we only handle single-level comprehensions
+        if len(comp_node.generators) != 1:
+            return None
+        
+        comp = comp_node.generators[0]
+        
+        # We don't handle comprehensions with conditions (ifs) for now
+        if comp.ifs:
+            return None
+        
+        # Create a for loop
+        # for target in iter:
+        #     assert elt (for all) or if elt: break (for any)
+        
+        self.statements = []
+        self.variables = []
+        self.variable_counter = itertools.count()
+        self.stack = []
+        self.on_failure = []
+        
+        # Create the loop body
+        loop_body = []
+        
+        if all_any_name == 'all':
+            # For all(), we assert each element
+            # Create an assert statement for the element
+            self.push_format_context()
+            test_res, test_expl = self.visit(comp_node.elt)
+            self.push_format_context()
+            
+            # Create the assertion
+            negation = ast.UnaryOp(ast.Not(), test_res)
+            fail_body = self.on_failure
+            loop_body.append(ast.If(negation, fail_body, []))
+            
+            # Create failure message
+            if assert_.msg:
+                assertmsg = self.helper("_format_assertmsg", assert_.msg)
+                explanation = "
+>assert " + test_expl
+            else:
+                assertmsg = ast.Str("")
+                explanation = "assert " + test_expl
+            
+            template = ast.BinOp(assertmsg, ast.Add(), ast.Str(explanation))
+            msg = self.pop_format_context(template)
+            fmt = self.helper("_format_explanation", msg)
+            err_name = ast.Name("AssertionError", ast.Load())
+            exc = ast_Call(err_name, [fmt], [])
+            if sys.version_info[0] >= 3:
+                raise_ = ast.Raise(exc, None)
+            else:
+                raise_ = ast.Raise(exc, None, None)
+            fail_body.append(raise_)
+            self.pop_format_context(None)
+            
+        else:  # any
+            # For any(), we need to check if any element is truthy
+            # We'll create a variable to track if we found a truthy element
+            found_var = self.variable()
+            loop_body.append(ast.Assign([ast.Name(found_var, ast.Store())], ast.NameConstant(False)))
+            
+            self.push_format_context()
+            test_res, test_expl = self.visit(comp_node.elt)
+            
+            # if elt: found_var = True; break
+            inner_body = [
+                ast.Assign([ast.Name(found_var, ast.Store())], ast.NameConstant(True)),
+                ast.Break()
+            ]
+            loop_body.append(ast.If(test_res, inner_body, []))
+            self.pop_format_context(None)
+            
+            # After the loop, assert that we found at least one truthy element
+            # This will be added after the for loop
+        
+        # Create the for loop
+        for_loop = ast.For(
+            target=comp.target,
+            iter=comp.iter,
+            body=loop_body,
+            orelse=[]
+        )
+        
+        self.statements.append(for_loop)
+        
+        if all_any_name == 'any':
+            # Add assertion after the loop
+            fail_body = []
+            negation = ast.UnaryOp(ast.Not(), ast.Name(found_var, ast.Load()))
+            self.statements.append(ast.If(negation, fail_body, []))
+            
+            # Create failure message
+            if assert_.msg:
+                assertmsg = self.helper("_format_assertmsg", assert_.msg)
+                explanation = "
+>assert any(...)"
+            else:
+                assertmsg = ast.Str("")
+                explanation = "assert any(...)"
+            
+            template = ast.BinOp(assertmsg, ast.Add(), ast.Str(explanation))
+            msg = self.pop_format_context(template)
+            fmt = self.helper("_format_explanation", msg)
+            err_name = ast.Name("AssertionError", ast.Load())
+            exc = ast_Call(err_name, [fmt], [])
+            if sys.version_info[0] >= 3:
+                raise_ = ast.Raise(exc, None)
+            else:
+                raise_ = ast.Raise(exc, None, None)
+            fail_body.append(raise_)
+        
+        # Clear temporary variables
+        if self.variables:
+            variables = [ast.Name(name, ast.Store()) for name in self.variables]
+            clear = ast.Assign(variables, _NameConstant(None))
+            self.statements.append(clear)
+        
+        # Fix line numbers
+        for stmt in self.statements:
+            set_location(stmt, assert_.lineno, assert_.col_offset)
+        
+        return self.statements
